title: Anthropic 内部研究显示初级技术岗位占比下降，AI Agent 工时达员工六倍
content:
Anthropic 内部研究显示初级技术岗位占比下降，AI Agent 工时达员工六倍
Anthropic has nearly stopped hiring junior staff because AI agents now work six times as many hours
Anthropic 发布内部研究称，技术部门初级岗位占比从 2025 年初的 21% 降至 14%，新招初级占比从 27% 降至 9%，空缺初级职位降至 6%，非技术部门基本稳定。
Anthropic 内部数据显示初级技术岗位占比明显下降而 Agent 工时升至人力六倍，报道还保留了研究自身对数据局限性的说明。
Anthropic 在技术岗位中招聘的初级员工越来越少，而其 AI 智能体记录的工作时长却在持续攀升。
根据这家 AI 公司发布的一项内部研究，自 2025 年初以来，技术部门初级岗位的占比从 21% 降至 14%。新员工的降幅更大，初级员工占比从 27% 跌至仅 9%。从 2025 年 12 月开始，开放的初级岗位数量下降尤为急剧。
Anthropic 将其归因于自家 AI 智能体能力的不断增强。到 2026 年 8 月，这些智能体记录的工作时长已是人类员工的六倍。编写代码和查找漏洞等任务越来越多地被交给 Claude。在 Claude 承担最复杂工作的岗位上，初级招聘的降幅最大。
据 Anthropic 称，各部门的生产力均有提升。工程师提交的代码提交量达到 5.1 倍，数据科学家运行的查询量达到 3.1 倍，法务团队处理的合同量达到 3.1 倍。销售团队成交的交易量达到 1.7 倍，招聘人员招聘的人数达到 1.4 倍，会计处理的发票量达到 1.4 倍。
不过，该研究本身也承认，Anthropic 是一个特例。它是一家极度依赖 AI 的软件公司，其结果难以直接套用到更广泛的经济体上。业务的快速增长和对 AI 工具的自愿采用也可能使数据出现偏差。到目前为止，更广泛的经济体尚未显示出 AI 带来的可衡量生产力提升。
如今初级岗位减少，意味着未来专家也会减少
北约特种作战大学的研究员 Nolan Lovett 最近在一篇研究论文中描述了“认知公地悲剧”。当个别企业用 AI 取代入门级岗位时，它们享受效率提升带来的收益，而成本则分摊到所有日后需要经验丰富人才的人身上。Anthropic 正符合这一模式。
熟练的专业人士只有通过在如今正在消失的初级岗位上多年实践才能成长起来。Lovett 认为，全面影响要到 2030 至 2045 年才会显现，因为当下可用的专家是在 5 到 20 年前培养出来的。软件工程、金融分析和法律研究是受影响最大的领域。
不过，Lovett 的预测只有在未来人类仍从事这类工作的前提下才成立。而这大概是 Anthropic 自己都不曾预期的：该公司过去曾提出，程序员和呼叫中心工作人员最终需要转向电工或护士等职业。

report.summary: Anthropic's internal study shows junior technical roles fell from 21% to 14% of its tech workforce while its AI agents logged six times more work hours than human staff.
report.background: Anthropic is both a builder and a heavy user of AI coding agents, so its internal data doubles as an early signal of how agentic AI reshapes hiring. Since Claude Code and similar tools became reliable at writing code, finding bugs, and running multi-step tasks, companies have debated whether AI substitutes for or augments junior developers — the classic entry-level tasks of boilerplate coding, test writing, and research are exactly what agents do well. Meanwhile, economists have found little measurable productivity gain across the wider economy, making Anthropic an outlier rather than a preview. The report also revives a structural worry: if firms stop training beginners, the pipeline of experienced specialists that everyone depends on may quietly erode over the next decade.
key_points: The numbers: junior roles in Anthropic's technical org dropped from 21% to 14% of headcount since early 2025; among new hires the fall was steeper, from 27% to 9%, and open junior positions shrank to 6%. Non-technical departments stayed roughly flat, suggesting the shift is specific to work agents can do.

Agent usage scaled fast: by August 2026 Anthropic's AI agents logged six times the working hours of human employees, and the decline in junior hiring was sharpest in teams where Claude handles the most complex tasks — implying substitution, not just slower growth.

Productivity gains were broad but uneven: engineers' code commits hit 5.1x, data scientists' queries 3.1x, legal contracts 3.1x, sales deals 1.7x, recruiting 1.4x and invoices 1.4x. These are self-reported internal metrics, not independently audited benchmarks.

Anthropic itself cautions the study is not generalizable: it is an AI-native software company with explosive growth and voluntary tool adoption, and the broader economy still shows no measurable AI productivity lift. The data may reflect selection effects as much as substitution.

A researcher cited in the report warns of a 'tragedy of the cognitive commons': firms capture efficiency gains from replacing entry-level roles while the cost — a missing generation of experts — is spread across everyone who will need them in 2030-2045.
report.impact: For the AI industry, the report is a credibility test: a leading lab is effectively publishing evidence that its own products reduce demand for junior talent, which will intensify scrutiny of vendor-claimed productivity. For developers, the entry ramp is narrowing — the apprenticeship tasks that built senior engineers (boilerplate, debugging, test writing) are precisely what agents absorb, pushing juniors toward review, architecture, and agent supervision skills earlier. For regular users, cheaper and faster software, legal, and support work is the near-term upside; the longer-term risk is a thinner pool of seasoned experts and rising premiums for judgment-heavy roles. Expect more firms to publish or be pushed to disclose similar internal data.
report.tools: To follow this shift hands-on, try Claude Code and the Claude Agent SDK for agentic coding workflows, plus open-source alternatives like OpenHands and Aider for self-hosted agents. Cursor and GitHub Copilot show the IDE-integrated path, while SWE-bench and Terminal-Bench offer benchmarks for judging agent capability. For tracking labor-market effects, watch Anthropic's Economic Index, Stanford HAI's AI Index, and St. Louis Fed wage data on entry-level tech roles.
